Bikeways This map depicts types of bikeways, each with specific characteristics: Bike paths provide a paved right-of-way that is completely separated from the street. They are typically shared with pedestrians and often called mixed-use paths. Separated bike lanes use parked cars, raised curbs, or other vertical elements to separate bicyclists from vehicular traffic. Bike boulevards are routes on residential streets that prioritize through trips for bicyclists. They include pavement markings, wayfinding signs, and traffic-calming elements. Buffered bike lanes are striped on streets and designated specifically for bicycle travel. They have a painted buffer zone that gives bicyclists more space between moving traffic and parked cars. Bike lanes are striped on streets and designated specifically for bicycle travel. Bike routes are marked with signs and/or pavement markings, and may have bicyclists sharing lanes with drivers on busier streets. Proposed bikeways, a subset of streets designated for improvements by Oakland’s bike plan, may provide useful connections because of lower traffic volumes or wider travel lanes. Wayfinding This map features 150+ destinations being supported on Oakland’s bicycle guide signs. These destinations include downtown, adjoining cities, transit stations, commercial districts, parks and recreation centers, landmarks, colleges, hospitals, and high schools. The signs follow the general conventions of highway guide signs to communicate information in a clear, consistent, and space-efficient format. For more information, see www.oaklandbikes.info/design.
